study type: secondary analysis of a cluster randomized controlled trial
exposure: multifaceted intervention to improve quality of obstetrical care and reduce Caesarean section rates
provision of feedback to health professionals
implementation of best practices to reduce CS rates
outcome: rate of vaginal birth after Caesarean (VBAC)
cohort: The study included 105,351 women who delivered during pre- and post-intervention periods, with a focus on the 12,493 (11.9%) who had a previous Caesarean section.
finding: A multifaceted intervention aimed at reducing Caesarean section rates did not significantly impact VBAC rates or maternal and neonatal morbidity.
mod_finding: The intervention showed no significant impact on trial of labour or VBAC rates in women with one previous CS, but it reduced the rate of trial of labour in women with more than one previous CS.
